title.narrative: Income Support Program for the Poorest

description.narrative: The Project Development Objective is to provide income support to the poorest mothers in selected Upazilas, while (i) increasing the mothers use of child nutrition and cognitive development services, and (ii) enhancing local level government capacity to deliver safety nets.

The objective of the Income Support Program for the Poorest Project for Bangladesh is to provide income support to the poorest mothers in selected Upazilas, while (i) increasing the mothers? use of child nutrition and cognitive development services, and (ii) enhancing local level government capacity to deliver safety nets. The project has three components. (1) Cash transfers for beneficiary mother?s components will finance quarterly cash transfers to eligible households. (2) Enhancing local level government capacity component will provide the necessary inputs to Local Government Division (LGD) to facilitate the implementation of the proposed cash transfers. This will include strengthening the capacity of: (i) Union Parishads to develop the beneficiary list based on the Bangladesh Poverty Database (BPD) being developed by SID, and supervise their enrolment into ISPP; (ii) Community Clinics (CCs) to deliver the ANC and GMP services, and the CNCD awareness sessions; and (iii) Union Post Offices (UPOs) to make electronic payments to beneficiaries using the Postal Cash Cards (PCCs) upon compliance with co-responsibilities. (3) Monitoring and evaluation component will be critical to assess progress in achieving the project?s objectives, and the impact of cash transfers on household poverty and on CNCD outcomes. This component will thus provide the necessary inputs to help LGD monitor ISPP beneficiary selection, enrolment, compliance with co-responsibilities, payments, case management as well as any grievances or appeals. To facilitate these activities, this component will develop an automated Management Information System (MIS) by building on the existing Shombhob Pilot MIS.

title.narrative: Number of Unions/municipal wards on which periodic beneficiary spot checks surveys conducted

comment.narrative: <p><strong>Target not achieved. </strong>Spot checks had been carried out throughout Project implementation until March 2020.While the periodic targets for this indicator were partially met during FY19 (Target = 20, Achievement = 19) and exceeded in FY18 (Target = 0, Achievement = 4) & FY20 (Target = 20, Achievement = 45), the project failed to meet this target for the final two years – FY21 and FY22 because no additional spot-checks were conducted after FY20 due to COVID-19 lockdown measure which suspended all field-level activities. After activities resumed, there were delays in contracting a new firm.</p>

title.narrative: Proportion of ISPP beneficiaries receiving at least 50 percent of the maximum benefit amount

comment.narrative: <p><strong>Target exceeded. </strong>During FY22,<strong> </strong>100% (target 70%) of the beneficiaries received at least 50% of the maximum benefit amount. In fact, the program has been continuously exceeding the annual targets for this indicator since FY18. This indicates strong overall performance from the stakeholders involved in providing ANC, GMP and CNCD services (i.e., BRAC and Community Clinics), and facilitating cash transfers (BPO, Union Parishad Offices, UNO, SPA & SPS among others). However, spot checks reports, beneficiary assessment report, aide memoires and BRAC’s contract completion report mentioned a few challenges (i.e., limited capacity of community clinics, issues related to biometric verification etc.) during implementation.</p>

title.narrative: Unions maintaining a single beneficiary registry of at least five safety net programs

comment.narrative: <p><strong>Target exceeded. </strong>443 unions currently maintain a single registry of at least five safety net programs against the target of 100 and revised target of 325 unions. The indicator mainly started to make progress after the first restructuring in 2018. In FY19, the achievement was 450% above the annual target (achievement = 275 unions, target = 50 unions). This achievement combined with a two-year time extension spurred an upward revision of the targets during second restructuring in 2019. Even after the upward revision of targets, achievement of this indicator did not slow down and continued to overshoot the annual targets till FY22.</p>

<p><strong>Target exceeded. </strong>This indicator exceeded its target (of 400,000 beneficiaries) by approximately 50%. Since all the beneficiaries of ISPP-Jawtno are female, the achievement status of the second sub-indicator (number of female beneficiaries) is the same as well. However, it is important to note that program struggled to meet the annual targets until FY21 due to various factors such as – delays in procurement critical services, unavailability of NHD and, COVID-19 pandemic. Nonetheless, the program picked up its pace again in FY21 and was able to exceed the end target thanks to the strong commitment, flexibility due a two-year extension and prudent decision-making exhibited by the WB task team and LGD.</p>

title.narrative: Proportion of eligible households in the bottom two expenditure quintiles of the NHD that are enrolled as beneficiaries

comment.narrative: <p><strong>Target exceeded. </strong>75% (target 70%) of the eligible households, that are enrolled as beneficiaries of ISPP-Jawtnoprogram during FY22, fall within the bottom two expenditure quintiles of the NHD. In fact, this indicator has been consistently exceeding the target since FY18. It is important to note that the program had to rely on the results of ‘Poverty Score Survey’, commissioned by WB, in order to measure the achievement of this indicator because NHD was unavailable. In order to ensure comparability of the survey results with poverty scores from NHD, the Poverty Score Survey was designed based on the Proxy Means Testing (PMT) methodology that is being used for the NHD itself.</p>

title.narrative: Proportion of ISPP beneficiary pregnant women who fulfill ANC co-responsibility

comment.narrative: <p><strong>Target exceeded. </strong>During FY22, 81% (target 70%) of the ISPP beneficiary pregnant women and mothers fulfilled ANCco-responsibility. However, Attainment of ANC coverage for the pregnant women remained consistently below the annual targets until FY22. While COVID-19 induced service discontinuation (July – December 2020 and June 2021) contributed to the low coverage in FY21, there were various other factors that resulted in the underachievement of annual targets till FY20. These include: i) an extended period of lead time (4-5 months) between enrollment and service integration leading to - many women starting ANC visits during their 3rd trimester thus not having the time to fulfil ANC co-responsibility because most of them either got delivered or moved to their paternal home for delivery before completing required number of check-ups, while many women even completed their pregnancy duringthe lead time between enrollment and service integration; ii) Inadequate number and capacity of community clinics; iii) settlement outside of the catchment area due to engagement with income generation and other activities; iv) non-integration with service coverage due to mismatched fingerprint or not receiving cash card, and v) reluctance to attend service sessions due to individual factors including inadequate health seeking among others. Nonetheless, new enrollments during FY22, after the COVID induced restrictions were lifted, helped the program exceed the end target for this indicator.</p>

title.narrative: Proportion of implementing Upazilas processing grievance cases

comment.narrative: <p><strong>Target exceeded. </strong>In FY22, 85% of implementing Upazilas processed grievance against the target of 40%. It is also important to note that this indicator itself was revised from “Implementing Unions/municipal wards addressing grievance cases” to the current form (currently it takes Upazilas as unit of measurement rather than unions / wards) during the first restructuring in 2018. The targets were also revised downwards for FY18 (from 30% to 0%), FY19 (from 45% to 0%) and FY20 (from 60% to 30%). Afterwards, the second restructuring in 2019 increased the end target from 30% (FY20) to 40% (FY22) considering the two-year time extension. However, the project actually outperformed the targets since FY19. The achievement status for each FY19, FY20 & FY21 were 100% (target 0%), 60% (target 30%), and 62% (target 40%) respectively. During FY20 & FY21, when services were discontinued,and cash transfers were made unconditional due to COVID-19 related mobility restrictions, number of grievances decreased because grievances were primarily related to payment issues or beneficiaries not understanding the correlation between their compliance with co-responsibilities and the amount of transfer they received. On the other hand, the number of grievances increased after services resumed since the second half of FY21 and this caused the percentage of upazilas processing grievances for FY22 to rise.</p>

title.narrative: Proportion of ISPP beneficiary mothers who fulfill quarterly GMP co-responsibility

comment.narrative: <p><strong>Target exceeded. </strong>At the endline (FY22),<strong> </strong>91% beneficiary mothers under the ISPP program fulfilled their monthly GMP co-responsibilities against the target of 70%. The unconditional nature of ISPP cash transfers since March2020 and other pandemic induced relaxations in conditionality may have played a role in the program exceeding the target for this indicator in FY22.</p>

title.narrative: Proportion of ISPP beneficiary mothers who fulfill monthly GMP co-responsibility

comment.narrative: <p><strong>Target exceeded. </strong>At the end-line (FY22),<strong> </strong>94% beneficiary mothers under the ISPP program fulfilled their monthly GMP co-responsibilities against the target of 70%. It outperformed the annual targets for this indicator almost every year, except FY21, when the delivery of monthly GMP sessions were discontinued for a long period (July – December 2020 andJune 2021) due to COVID-19 related mobility restrictions. However, it is important to note that, unconditional nature of ISPP cash transfers since March 2020 and other pandemic induced relaxations in conditionality (i.e., beneficiaries only needed to attend 1 GMPsession per quarter to fulfil this co-responsibility, instead of 1 GMP session each month) may have played a role in the program exceeding the target for this indicator in FY22. However, BRAC – the CNCD service firm – in its contract completion report notes that the results could have been better if the service delivery capacity (human resource and equipment) had been better at community clinics.</p>

title.narrative: Proportion of ISPP beneficiary pregnant women and mothers who fulfill CNCD co-responsibility

comment.narrative: <p><strong>Target exceeded. </strong>During FY22,<strong> </strong>94% of the ISPP beneficiary pregnant women and mothers fulfilledCNCD co-responsibility against the target of 70%. The achievement becomes even more significant when we consider that during FY21 & FY22, the beneficiaries would have received the cash transfer even if they had not attended these sessions because the cash transfers were unconditional during this period. This suggests that these sessions were highly appreciated by beneficiaries irrespective of the cash transfer component because it provided a platform for the women, while children enjoyed playing with toys and socializing with their own peers. The fact that over 90% beneficiaries attended BRAC-organized CNCD sessions during Jan-Mar 2022 even thoughthere was no cash incentive, further supports aforementioned notion. Such success in inciting positive behavioral change amongthe beneficiaries can be attributed to – strong commitment and performance shown by the CNCD Services firm (BRAC), ISPP-PMU, and local administrative and health authorities. Another key contributor, here, was the initiative to build the awareness of community beneficiaries since this helped create demand for these sessions.</p>

title.narrative: Process evaluation of project cycle conducted

comment.narrative: <p><strong>Original target not achieved / could not be evaluated.</strong> While the program met its annual targets for this indicator till March 2020, no additional evaluations activities were carried out after that time due to COVID-19 lockdown measure which suspended all field-level activities. After activities resumed, there were delays in contracting a new firm. The target was formally revised after 2020.</p>

title.narrative: Dissemination of monitoring and evaluation reports on annual basis

comment.narrative: <p><strong>Target not achieved.</strong> The PAD suggests that the ISPP-PMU were expected prepare and disseminate M&E reports based on MIS generated data. In practice, the MIS was a key source of basic data, and periodic reports were generated to update the RF. Spot checks / process evaluation reports were used as the basis to hold a stakeholder workshop and disseminate findings. Dissemination of M&E reports were carried out annually at the end of the FY. However, the contract with the firm responsible for preparing spot-checks and process evaluation reports expired in 2020. Due to the Project's inability to procure a new firm in 2021, there were no further dissemination events held during FY21 & FY22 (which is why indicator appears as 'no' at completion although dissemination occurred in previous FYs).</p>
